title: Cardiac mortality prediction in patients undergoing PCI based on real and synthetic data
summary: Compares five synthetic oversamplers on a registry of patients after percutaneous coronary intervention, measuring not only discrimination but calibration and confidence for each of six downstream classifiers, and finds that oversampling changes model behaviour rather than merely improving scores: recall rises at the cost of accuracy and calibration, and several generators are actively harmful. Three of the five oversamplers are SDV synthesizers, CTGAN, TVAE and GaussianCopula, each trained on the minority class and reported as its own block of results.
evidence: the synthetic data generation section describes TVAE [15] as assuming a Gaussian latent structure and Gaussian mixtures for continuous variables, CTGAN [15] as an adversarial framework for tabular data effective on imbalanced categorical features, and GaussianCopula as a copula method capturing linear dependence, reference [15] being Xu et al. (2019); the results and calibration tables carry separate blocks for models with TVAE, GAN and Gaussian Copula oversampling alongside ARF and TabSyn, and the discussion concludes that ARF and GAN oversampling are the most effective while TVAE and Gaussian Copula are less effective and often detrimental. The paper names no library for the generators, but the model names match the SDV synthesizer classes

title: Generating High-quality Privacy-preserving Synthetic Data
summary: Proposes a post-processing pipeline that can be slotted after any tabular generator, patching the categorical modes a generator collapses and then filtering samples that sit too close to a training record, and evaluates the trade-off it produces on a joint fidelity, utility and privacy protocol across three benchmarks. The pipeline is built and measured entirely on CTGAN and TVAE, tuned per dataset by Bayesian search, with the SDV implementation of the correct attribution probability supplying the privacy score.
evidence: the evaluation design states that for each of Credit Default, Adult and Cardio the authors train CTGAN and TVAE and then apply mode-patching and the epsilon-ANY filter as post-processing, the stated goal being not a new generator but a pipeline that can be slotted after CTGAN, TVAE or future models; the privacy section states that the SDV implementation returns the correct attribution probability protection score, which is reported as a percentage and summarised by median across attributes; Table II lists the tuned CTGAN generator and discriminator learning rates, embedding and hidden dimensions per dataset, and SDGym is cited as the early fidelity and utility benchmark that neglected privacy

title: CausalWrap: Model-Agnostic Causal Constraint Wrappers for Tabular Synthetic Data
summary: Observes that generators trained to match an observational joint distribution can score well on column-wise utility while distorting causal effect estimates, and fits a post-hoc correction module that pulls a trained generator's samples toward a partially known causal structure, evaluated on synthetic structural causal models of three kinds and on a MIMIC-IV intensive-care cohort against an oracle sampler. Two of the three wrapped base generators are SDV, CTGAN and TVAE, each trained in its standard implementation before the wrapper is fitted.
evidence: the experimental setup states that three base generators spanning the GAN, diffusion and VAE families are wrapped, CTGAN [Xu et al., 2019], TabDDPM and TVAE [Xu et al., 2019], each trained using its standard implementation with CausalWrap then fitted as a post-hoc correction module on top; the results table reports per-generator causal error and the change under the wrapper for CTGAN and TVAE across linear-Gaussian, non-linear additive and mixed-type structural causal models against an oracle sampler. The related-work section separately places Causal-TGAN as injecting a known causal graph into CTGAN's conditional generation, which is a distinct approach from the post-hoc wrapper proposed here

title: Data Augmentation via Causal-Residual Bootstrapping
summary: Augments a small tabular dataset by resampling residuals along a known or estimated causal graph, so that added points respect the causal structure rather than only the observed joint distribution, and reports lower downstream error than both a no-augmentation baseline and generative augmenters, several of which prove worse than not augmenting at all. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generative augmentation baselines run at 100 training samples across the reported error tables.
evidence: the experimental section compares causal-residual bootstrapping against SMOTE-style and generative augmenters, listing CTGAN as the GAN-based approach for tabular data and TVAE (Xu et al., 2019) as the variational autoencoder adapted for tables, alongside TabDDPM, ARF and NFLOW, and states the non-causal augmenters are included to check that gains come from causal structure rather than extra points; Figure 4 and the per-variable and per-dataset error tables report CTGAN and TVAE rows throughout, with both recorded as performing worse than no augmentation in the known-graph setting. The paper miscites CTGAN to Bowles et al. (2018) while citing TVAE correctly to Xu et al. (2019)

title: A Systematic Framework for Tabular Data Disentanglement
summary: Sets out a formal framework for tabular data disentanglement, defining the extraction and extrapolation queries a data owner issues, the external knowledge available, and the utility and privacy objectives against which a latent representation is scored, so that otherwise unrelated approaches can be read as instances of one flow. CTGAN and TVAE are named as two of the existing approaches the framework subsumes, cited for conditional generation under specified conditions and for latent-representation learning respectively, with mode collapse and generation quality given as their limitations; neither is run.
evidence: the abstract names factor analysis, CT-GAN and VAE as the existing tabular disentanglement methods whose scalability, mode collapse and extrapolation limitations motivate the framework; section 1 repeats CT-GAN [32] as conditionally generating synthetic data under specified conditions with limitations in efficiency and overall quality, and argues that factor analysis, CT-GAN and VAE can be seen as parts of one general disentanglement flow; a later section groups TVAE [32] with Tabsyn, Switchtab and VAEGMM as following the generic latent-representation approach. Reference [32] is Xu et al. The paper is formal throughout and reports no experiments

title: Active Tabular Augmentation via Policy-Guided Diffusion Inpainting
summary: Argues that distributional fidelity is the wrong objective for augmentation under data scarcity and instead selects what to synthesise by a policy that targets where the current learner is weakest, inpainting the chosen regions with a diffusion model over rounds, and reports gains over augmenters that optimise fidelity alone. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the seven compared augmentation methods, run from their official implementations at the same synthetic budget and data splits as the rest.
evidence: the baselines paragraph lists seven augmentation methods and names the VAE-based TVAE (Xu et al., 2019) and the GAN-based CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) among them, alongside SMOTE, ARF, SPADA, TabDDPM and TabDiff; appendix D.3 states that official implementations with recommended defaults are used and that all methods share the same synthetic budget of 500 samples and the same splits; Tables 9 and 10 and the main accuracy table report CTGAN and TVAE columns at every scarcity level, with related work crediting them as the early methods that transform mixed-type features into a continuous space

title: TabQueryBench: A Query-Centric Benchmark for Synthetic Tabular Data
summary: Scores synthetic tables by whether analytical queries return the same answers on them as on the real data, rather than by distance between distributions, and shows the two can diverge: a generator can look strong on distance metrics while collapsing the support a filtered or grouped query depends on, with high-cardinality columns and local conditional queries the sharpest failures. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the eleven generators put through the benchmark, each packaged and tuned over epochs, batch size and embedding and hidden dimensions.
evidence: the model table places CTGAN [72] and TVAE [72] in the GAN and VAE families among eleven generators covering Bayesian, tree, diffusion, transformer and flow-matching approaches, reference [72] being Xu et al.; the hyperparameter section states that each model is packaged in its own Docker image and that CTGAN and TVAE were tuned over epochs, batch size, embedding dimension and hidden-layer dimensions with CTGAN at 50 to 200 epochs; the results report CTGAN generating 19,630 of the 96,777 distinct values in a high-cardinality column and TVAE scoring well on Jensen-Shannon divergence while compressing the support a grouped aggregate needs. SDGym is cited as a prior fixed-suite benchmark, referenced to docs.sdv.dev/sdgym, but is not run
needs: integration for a benchmark paper is a convention gap: nothing is proposed here, so the eleven generators are evaluation subjects rather than baselines against a contribution, which makes baseline_only a poor fit; recorded api_user at importance 3 because CTGAN and TVAE are run but are two rows of eleven

title: Measuring the Dependency Gap: Diagnosing Inter-Column Fidelity in Tabular Generative Models
summary: Shows that a fully factorized table, with every column shuffled independently so that all inter-column dependency is destroyed, still passes the commonly reported linear classifier two-sample test on four benchmarks, and replaces it with a gradient-boosted test whose score decomposes into marginal, dependency and numerical-categorical cross terms read against zero-dependency and oracle references. The metrics shown to be blind are SDMetrics': the logistic detection score and the pairwise Trend similarity are computed and reported throughout as the foil against which the new diagnostic is set.
evidence: the related-work section states that the dominant fidelity metrics are the column-wise and pairwise Shape and Trend similarities together with a detection score, as packaged by widely used libraries such as SDMetrics (Patki et al., 2016), whose detection metric trains a logistic-regression discriminator; section 3 reports the linear C2ST as the SDMetrics logistic-detection score and Trend as the SDMetrics pairwise column-correlation similarity, both carried through the results only to demonstrate their blindness, the fully factorized reference scoring 0.995 to 1.000 on the linear test and 0.69 to 0.78 on Trend; section 5 attributes a Trend discrepancy on one dataset to a plausible data-split or SDMetrics-version difference, which establishes that the library itself was run. CTGAN appears only as one citation in a list of GAN-based generators and is not evaluated
